title: On-call & Incident Response: Playbooks, Runbooks, Postmortems, and Comms Templates
author: Priya Nair
body:
Overview:

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's on-call and incident response standards: the incident lifecycle, standardized runbook format, postmortem requirements, on-call rotation rules, game day guidance, and canonical status page and customer communications templates. It is intended for SREs, service owners, on-call engineers, support, and product on-call participants.

Goals:
- Restore customer-visible service quickly and safely.
- Minimize blast radius and preserve data integrity.
- Communicate clearly and proactively to internal stakeholders and customers.
- Capture learnings in reproducible postmortems and action items.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood-hosted services and customer-facing endpoints (API, Console, Dedicated control plane). Private deployments follow the same playbooks but may have additional contractual constraints.

Key roles and responsibilities:
- Incident Commander (IC): owns triage, major decisions, and postmortem initiation. Typically the primary on-call engineer for the affected service.
- Scribe / Notes: records timeline, actions, commands, and decisions.
- Communications Lead (Comms): crafts internal and external messages (status page, customer comms). Often a member of SRE or support.
- Tech Leads / SMEs: provide deep-dive diagnostics and mitigation.
- Incident Responder(s): run mitigation steps and fixes.
- Executive liaison: briefed for Sev1/major-impact incidents.

Severity definitions and SLAs (summary):
- Sev 1 (Critical): System-wide outage or API unavailability affecting >10% of customers or high business impact. Target MTTA < 5 minutes; target MTR < 60 minutes for partial mitigation.
- Sev 2 (High): Major feature degraded or significant performance impact. Target MTTA < 15 minutes; target MTR < 4 hours.
- Sev 3 (Medium): Partial loss of functionality or single-customer impact with workarounds. Target MTTA < 2 hours; target MTR < 72 hours.
- Sev 4 (Low): Non-urgent bugs, feature regressions, or operational tasks. Addressed in backlog.

Incident lifecycle (short):
1) Detection and acknowledgement
   - Alert routes to #oncall-alerts Slack and PagerDuty. On-call engineer must acknowledge within severity-specific MTTA.
   - Use monitoring runbooks to confirm signal (metrics, logs, tracing).
2) Triage (IC assigned)
   - IC declares severity and kickoff. Record basic metadata: service, start_time, observed_impacts, pagerduty_incident_id, slack-thread-link.
3) Mitigate
   - Execute targeted runbook steps. If no runbook, use fallbacks: scale, rollback, revert recent deploy, or route traffic away.
4) Communicate
   - Internal: update #incidents, post timeline in incident channel every 30 minutes until stable.
   - External: publish status updates on status.redwood.inference (see templates).
5) Resolve and recover
   - Confirm system healthy, monitor for recurrence for 1-2x expected cooldown window.
6) Postmortem and follow-up
   - IC or owner opens postmortem within 48 hours of recovery. Assign action items with owners and due dates.

Standard runbook structure (single-file canonical format)
- Title
- Service / Component
- Owner / Primary on-call
- PagerDuty escalation policy ID
- Symptoms / How we detect (metric names & thresholds, log patterns, traces)
- Impact scope (who/what is affected)
- Quick triage checklist (first 10 minutes)
- Mitigation steps (ordered, safe to perform commands)
- Rollback / emergency rollback instructions
- Known good-state indicators (queries/metrics to validate)
- Post-incident actions and references
- Last updated and changelog

Example runbook snippet (API latency spike)
Symptoms:
- 95th percentile latency > 2s for 5m on service api-frontend-prod
- Increased 5xx rate > 1% sustained for 3m

Quick triage checklist:
1. Check dashboards: api-frontend-prod latency, upstream database latency, GPU queue length.
2. Confirm deploy windows: check deploy-log for recent releases in last 30 minutes.
3. Identify traces: open APM / tracing and find top error traces.

Mitigation (ordered):
1. If 5xx spike due to model worker OOMs, scale up worker pool by +2 instances: kubectl scale --replicas=<n+2> deployment/model-worker-prod -n prod
2. If latency due to DB throttling, apply read-only cache route or failover to replica (see DB failover runbook).
3. If new code deploy suspect, perform canary rollback using the deploy system rollback playbook.

Emergency rollback checklist (safe mode):
- Verify current commit and previous stable commit IDs
- Run rollback during low-traffic windows when possible or coordinate with Comms
- Post rollback, monitor error rates for 30 minutes before closing incident

Postmortem template (required for Sev 1/Sev 2 impacting customers):
- Title
- Incident lead (IC)
- Severity
- Start and end timestamps (UTC)
- Summary (one-paragraph customer-facing description)
- Impact (customers affected, API error rates, latency numbers, revenue/customer impact if known)
- Root cause analysis (timeline + technical cause)
- Contributing factors (process, monitoring gaps, test/CI issues)
- Immediate mitigations taken
- Long-term fixes / action items with owners and due dates
- Follow-ups (links to code changes, config changes, runbook updates)
- Lessons learned and prevention measures
- Attachments: logs, tracing screenshots, dashboards, PagerDuty timeline

Postmortem example summary:
"On 2026-01-11 03:14 UTC api-frontend experienced a spike in 5xx errors causing 28% of production requests to fail for ~47 minutes. Root cause: a regression in the request routing layer that caused malformed shard keys under specific traffic patterns. We rolled back the routing change and applied input validation at the gateway. Action items: add integration tests for shard key edge-cases (owner: Lina Zhang, due 2026-02-15), improve shard key dashboard (owner: Ethan Morales, due 2026-02-01)."

On-call rotation policy (summary):
- Primary on-call: 1-week rotation (Mon 00:00 UTC -> next Mon 00:00 UTC).
- Secondary/backup on-call: 2-week rotation; acts as escalation for complex incidents and provides coverage for holidays.
- Shift handover: outgoing primary must post a handover note in #oncall-handover channel with ongoing issues, background links, and any upcoming maintenance windows.
- Time off / swap: request swaps via PagerDuty and notify #oncall-schedule. All swaps must be recorded in the oncall calendar.
- PagerDuty rules: escalation after 5 min unacknowledged for Sev 1, 15 min for Sev 2.

Game days (recommended cadence):
- Quarterly cross-team game days (SRE + product + infra + backend) where we simulate a common incident scenario (e.g., control-plane outage, region failover, noisy neighbor GPU contention).
- Agenda: charting exercises (30m), inject & respond (60m), retrospective & action items (30m).
- Goals: validate runbooks, identify permission gaps, practice comms, and measure real MTTRs in a safe environment.

Status page and customer communications templates (canonical copy)
- Status page copy pattern (short live updates):
  - Title: "Partial API Degradation — Generations affected"
  - Summary: "We are investigating elevated error rates for text generation requests impacting a subset of customers. Our on-call team is actively investigating."
  - Impact: "Customers may experience increased 4xx/5xx errors and higher latency for model generations. Not all requests are affected."
  - Next steps: "We are identifying the root cause and will provide updates every 30 minutes."
  - Updated at: ISO timestamp

- Customer email template (for major incidents):
  Subject: Redwood Inference service incident impacting API generations — [SHORT STATUS]

  Body:
  Hello <Customer Name>,

  We are writing to let you know of an ongoing incident affecting Redwood Inference API generations.

  Timeline:
  - Detected: 2026-01-11 03:14 UTC
  - Mitigated: 2026-01-11 04:01 UTC

  Impact:
  - A subset of requests experienced elevated 5xx errors and latency.
  - Customers using model "x" in region "y" were predominantly affected.

  Current status:
  - Services are restored; we are monitoring for recurrence.

  Next steps:
  - We will share a detailed postmortem within 48 hours with root cause and mitigation plan.

  If you have specific concerns or contractual questions, reply to this email or contact your Solutions Engineer.

  Regards,
  Redwood Inference Support Team

- Slack internal comms template (quick update in #incidents):
  @channel Incident: api-frontend-prod — Sev1 — 03:14 UTC
  Summary: Elevated 5xx + latency affecting ~28% of requests. IC: @pri. Updates every 15m. PagerDuty: PD-12345

Checklist for customer-facing comms:
- Keep language factual and neutral.
- No speculation on root cause.
- Provide clear next steps and ETA for next update.

Escalation matrix (short):
- After 15 minutes without mitigation for Sev1: page Team Lead and Eng Manager.
- After 30 minutes without mitigation: include VP Eng and Customer Success lead.
- After 60 minutes or if revenue impact identified: notify Executive liaison and Legal (if contractual/regulatory impact).

Monitoring and alerting standards (minimum):
- Every customer-facing service must have: error rate, latency p50/p95/p99, request volume, saturation metrics (CPU/memory/GPU queue), and a health-check probe.
- Alerts should be actionable (include links to runbooks and playbooks). Avoid alert storms: use aggregation windows and adaptive thresholds.

Runbook maintenance and ownership:
- Service owners must review runbooks at least quarterly or after each Sev1/2 incident.
- Major changes to runbooks must be recorded in the runbook changelog and approved by the SRE triage lead.

KPI and reporting:
- Track MTTA and MTTR per service monthly.
- Target: reduce Sev1 MTTR by 15% YoY.
- Include postmortem action completion rate in quarterly reliability review.

Appendix A — Commands and safe-execution rules:
- Always run destructive commands with a confirmation step. Prefix with: # SAFE-CHECK: owner, time, reason
- Example safe scaling command: kubectl scale deployment/model-worker-prod -n prod --replicas=5 # SAFE-CHECK: @oncall 2026-02-10 escalate to 5
- Example logs query: elasticsearch query: POST /api/_search {\"query\": {\"match\": {\"service\": \"api-frontend-prod\"}}} (include time range)

Appendix B — Example incident timeline format (for notes)
- 03:14 UTC — Alert triggered: 95p latency > 2s (monitoring)
- 03:16 UTC — IC assigned: @pri (ack), Slack channel created #inc-2026-01-11-api
- 03:20 UTC — Mitigation applied: scaled model-worker replicas +2
- 03:38 UTC — Rollback of routing change (candidate)
- 04:01 UTC — Error rates returned to baseline; monitoring window began
- 05:01 UTC — Incident declared resolved; postmortem required

Appendix C — Post-incident action item template (flat list)
- Action: Add integration test for shard key edge-cases | Owner: Lina Zhang | Due: 2026-02-15 | Status: open
- Action: Improve shard key dashboard & alerting | Owner: Ethan Morales | Due: 2026-02-01 | Status: open

Notes and references:
- See related runbooks: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks and /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks
- PagerDuty escalation policies are defined in the SRE team playbook.
- For private deployments, consult eng-private-deployments/customer-requirements-library for customer contractual SLAs.

Last reviewed: 2026-02-20 by Priya Nair.

If you find gaps or have improvements, please submit a change request in #oncall-improvements and update this document with a changelog entry.
